notes: §1985:XII.2.4 GR7: "Debugging lines are permitted within library text and pseudo-text" and their text words "participate in the matching rules as if the 'D' did not appear in the indicator area"; a debugging line is within pseudo-text if it begins after the opening delimiter and before the closing one. FixedFormConverter writes a D line as DebugLineCarrier plus its text in library text and in the COPY statement alike, TextWordScanner skips the carrier and scans the text, so ApplyReplacements matches its words with or without WITH DEBUGGING MODE; only after replacement does DebuggingLineRewriter hide the lines that are still debugging lines when the mode is off. Witness 1985-GR-XII_2_4-7 (a D line inside pseudo-text-1 and in library text, both modes). A pseudo-text-2 debugging line that replaces a word in the middle of a library line is written as a line of its own (ApplyReplacements, kb/Work PB5472), so the §1985:VI.7.3 check hides its words and no library text: witness pb5472-copy-debugging-line-replaces-mid-line prints [Q] with the mode, and pb5472-copy-debugging-line-replacement-needed (the line replaces a MOVE operand) is still COBOL7061.

next.reason: Amendment 1 (X3.23a-1989) only respelled 'pseudo-text-delimiter' as 'pseudo-text delimiter' twice, a typographical correction; the requirement is unchanged: §1985:XII.2.4 GR7 'Debugging lines are permitted within library text and pseudo-text', their text words 'participate in the matching rules as if the 'D' did not appear in the indicator area'. 2023 has no debugging lines: the phrase occurs nowhere in the standard, its fixed indicators (§2023:6.2.2) are the comment indicators, the continuation indicator and the space source indicator for 'any line that is not a comment line or a continuation line', and §2023:6.5 GR5 copies only 'a fixed-form line, contains a source indicator, and is not a continuation line'. No 2023 rule lets a 'D' line appear in library text or pseudo-text or has its words take part in matching.
